ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 limb (a) is met on the face of the bundle: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the identifier TRP-00527, and the trace's first fix and the trip record's start both read 2026-09-15T17:21:40+08:00, so the artifacts describe one and the same trip and the rider's threshold case is put on this trip's own evidence and no other.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the trace polyline, gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which here is 60.91 km; the 60.9 km carried on the trip_record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and the clause forbids citing it for the threshold test, so the excess must be measured from 60.91 km and not from any rounder figure.

This trip is RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 fixes the POL-RD-01 baseline at the matched-itinerary optimal stored on the trip record - 58.4 km for pooled itinerary POOL-7731, matched at 17:16 with 4 riders - and not at the rider's own solo-rider figure; the rider therefore does not put her threshold case on solo_optimal_distance_km, and asks that the ruling name the 58.4 km matched figure and the 32.4 km solo figure side by side, as that clause requires, so it is visible why a pooled plan is longer than her own trip.

Against that matched baseline the platform's own trace derivation measures the excess at 2.51 km, being 4.3% of the 58.4 km pooled plan; that excess is not zero, and the rider's complaint is not that pooling is long but that this driver drove further than even the route the platform itself planned for the pool, on a trip whose fare is metered on distance and time.

The platform's own money derivation on the fare_breakdown prices the optimal-route fare for this trip at 71.36 against a charged total of 76.88, and the 5.52 difference is exactly the metered cost of those 2.51 km and the 13 minutes driven beyond the 82-minute pooled plan; if the tribunal finds the excess meets POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary, the 5.52 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and the amount rounds up to 5.55 - the rider asks that this figure be the one on the record.

The rider is straight with the tribunal about the limit of her case: the same derivation puts that excess at 4.3% of the matched itinerary, which does not clear the 20% limb of POL-RD-01, and she accepts that on this record no distance-or-time refund under POL-RD-02 is available to her; she does not press the 88% excess that measuring against her own 32.4 km trip would yield, because POL-RD-12 says a claim measured against solo_optimal_distance_km fails on that ground alone, and she does not press the $174 figure in her complaint, because nothing in the bundle supports it - the ledger total is 76.88.

No rider instruction exists anywhere on this record that could shift any part of the driven distance onto the rider: the chat export for this trip carries zero messages (message_count 0, messages []), so the POL-RD-04 exoneration for a rider-requested detour or additional stop is unavailable for want of the chat instruction that clause requires, and the driver's 'pool routes are long' is an assertion with no artifact behind it for the 2.51 km at issue.

The only artifact that could have placed any part of the pooled routing on an external event is EV-ADVIS-00527-01, and it is MISSING: the pre-pass recorded issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight 0.0, noting that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window; the rider cites the absence itself - there is no traffic_advisory on this record under which POL-RD-03 could exonerate any stretch of the route.

Nothing is owed to the driver on the unbilled-distance limb: the fare_breakdown charges the rider for 60.9 km against a trace of 60.91 km and for the full 95.0 minutes driven, so the shortfall of more than 1.0 km that POL-RD-04 requires before DRIVER_COMPENSATION can arise does not exist.

The rider's own profile adds no corroboration requirement to her claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not engaged and the rider's excess is not put to any higher evidentiary standard on profile grounds; no field outside those the general policy names is relied on, per POL-GEN-01.

This was a RYDE_POOL trip, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 baseline is the MATCHED-ITINERARY optimal recorded on the trip record — 58.4 km — and not the solo-rider figure. The record shows the platform matched pooled itinerary POOL-7731 for 4 riders at 17:16, and trip_record.optimal_distance_km carries 58.4 km for that matched itinerary. The 32.4 km the rider is measuring against is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, which POL-RD-12 carries 'for reference only'. Distance spent collecting and setting down co-riders on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation, and a claim that measures excess against the solo figure 'has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone'.

Measured correctly against the matched-itinerary optimal, the excess is 2.51 km — the trace's 60.91 km against 58.4 km — which is 4.30% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH a percentage test (greater than 20% of optimal) AND an absolute test (greater than 0.8 km), and both must pass. The percentage fails by a factor of nearly five, so no deviation is ESTABLISHED and 'the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip'. Per POL-RD-01 the governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (60.91 km), not the rounded convenience copy trip_record.actual_distance_km (60.9 km), which may not be cited for the threshold test.

The trace the threshold test runs on is clean. The GPS artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 571 driver fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, and first and last fixes spanning the whole trip (17:21:40 to 18:56:40). It therefore satisfies none of the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) impairment limbs — no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval over 30 s — so the excess can be read directly off the trace and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger is engaged.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The excess is 2.51 km / 4.30%, below both limbs of the threshold, so the burden is not discharged and the analysis never reaches the driver's exculpatory clauses. The rider profile is not in play either: deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so the corroboration provision in POL-RD-08 is not triggered and the claim simply fails at the threshold.

No relocation re-quote is available under POL-RD-05: both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record and neither original_pickup nor original_dropoff is populated, so there is no amended endpoint and no amended_optimal_distance_km. The baseline therefore stays at the booked matched-itinerary optimal of 58.4 km, and no distance driven can be re-attributed.

There is likewise no rider-requested detour to weigh under POL-RD-04. The chat log for this trip is empty — message_count 0, no messages, not truncated — so there is no rider instruction and no chat_message.waypoint_hint on which the 200 m corroboration test could ever be run. The trip proceeded on the platform-matched pooled itinerary and nothing in the record shows the rider asking for, or being billed for, a detour of her own choosing.

The fare ledger carries no defect and no escalation trigger. The only charge lines are base fare 3.80, distance 45.68 and time 26.60 on the 60.9 km / 95 min actually driven, plus the 0.80 platform fee, summing to the 76.88 charged — every line has a counterpart in the GPS trace, ERP and tolls are 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, and no airport surcharge applies. There is no phantom gantry line under POL-RD-09(4) and therefore no POL-RD-10(8) trigger. POL-GEN-03 is explicit that NO_ACTION preserves the present state: the dispute is rider-filed, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so NO_ACTION leaves that charge standing — it is a win for the driver, not a restoration of anything.

The rider's demand is also arithmetically unreachable on the policy's own figures. Even on the counterfactual that a deviation existed, POL-RD-02 against this record (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 58.4 + 0.28 x 82.0, surge multiplier 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee, + 0 ERP, + 0 waiting, - 0 promo) gives a recomputed fare of 71.36 against a charged total of 76.88 — a refund of 5.52, rounded up to 5.55, or 7.2% of the charge. The contested amount is the entire 76.88 and no clause in this policy can produce it; the fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 is the ceiling on any distance or time remedy.

Because no deviation is established, let alone a MATERIAL one, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged. For completeness, even on the clause's own field pair the driver clears it by a wide margin: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, far below both the 3-flag test and the 5%-ratio test. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 asks for, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting one for the other.

That absence is citable and I cite it, but it decides nothing here: with the excess at 4.30% there is no deviation for a POL-RD-03 advisory to exonerate, and a weight-0.0 artifact can carry no fact in either direction. The rider cannot convert the platform's missing advisory into a deviation that the trace does not show.

The driver's account is the one the record supports. His statement — 'Pool routes are long; that's how pool works. The app splits the fare, not me' — is matched by the ledger: the 76.88 was metered by the platform at 0.75 per km and 0.28 per min on the pooled distance and time, with a 1.0 surge multiplier and no discretionary component the driver controls. The rider's grievance is with the pooled product she chose, and POL-RD-12 is the clause that says the pooled itinerary, not her solo route, is the lawful baseline for it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — the same answer in different words: the fare stands and no money moves.

WHY NO DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. This was a RYDE_POOL trip (TRP-00527). Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for measuring route length is the matched-itinerary optimal the platform computed at match time — 58.4 km for pooled itinerary POOL-7731, matched at 17:16 for 4 riders — and not the rider's own solo route of 32.4 km. I name both figures, as that clause requires, so the rider can see why a pooled plan is longer than her own trip: pooling is the product she chose, and distance spent collecting and setting down co-riders on a platform-matched itinerary is expressly excluded from any deviation.

Measured on the governing figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 60.91 km (POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern; the 60.9 km on the trip record is a rounded copy and may not be cited for the threshold test), the excess over the 58.4 km pooled baseline is 2.51 km, or 4.30% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute. The absolute limb passes; the percentage limb fails by a factor of nearly five. So no deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs the outcome to be NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised — except for a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4), which I checked for below and did not find.

The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07: 571 driver fixes at 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s, first/last fixes spanning the whole trip. The excess can be read directly off it and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 fails at the threshold limb, so the analysis never reaches the exculpatory clauses. Neither a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 (the chat log for this trip is empty — message_count 0, no messages) nor a relocation re-quote under POL-RD-05 (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, amended_optimal_distance_km is null) is available on this record.

THE MONEY. The charge is 76.88 = base fare 3.80 + distance 45.68 + time 26.60 + platform fee 0.80, with ERP and tolls 0.00, an empty gantry list and no airport surcharge. Every line has a counterpart in the trace, so there is no phantom line under POL-RD-09(4) and no POL-RD-10(8) trigger. For transparency only, POL-RD-02 run against the pooled optimal (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 58.4 + 0.28 x 82.0, surge multiplier 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee) gives a recomputed fare of 71.36 against the 76.88 charged — a 5.52 difference, 5.55 rounded up, or 7.2% of the charge. But that arithmetic only runs where a deviation is established, and it is not, so no refund issues and I state it only to show the ceiling on any distance-or-time remedy. The rider's complaint figure of $174 appears nowhere in the bundle; the amount actually charged, and the contested amount, is 76.88.

NO_ACTION leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they are. On a rider-filed dispute that means the charge stands; it is the driver's win on the fare.

CLAIMS ANSWERED. The rider's acceptance of the 4.30% figure and her concession that this does not clear the 20% limb are correct and dispose of her POL-RD-02 refund request (5.55) — a deviation is the precondition and it is absent. Her remaining points all hold and are accepted: the artifacts describe one trip (matching TRP-00527 and the 17:21:40 start on trace and trip record); the trace's 60.91 km governs; the pooled baseline is 58.4 km; no chat instruction shifts any distance to her; and her rider_profile counters deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so POL-RD-08's corroboration uplift is not triggered and she is held to no higher standard. The driver's points are accepted: the pooled baseline, the clean trace, the empty chat log, the null amendment fields, the fare lines, and the POL-RD-06 profile check, which the driver clears on the clause's own fields (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250, below both the 3-flag and 5%-ratio tests). The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 asks for and is not used — POL-GEN-01 confines that artifact to credibility weighting; it was flagged in the pre-pass and nothing on either profile beyond the clause-named counters has been relied on. No repeat-deviation pattern exists, so POL-RD-06(c) produces no conduct referral.

DISCLOSURE. EV-ADVIS-00527-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING — no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. A zero-weight artifact carries no fact and its absence is citable; it decides nothing in either direction, since with the excess at 4.30% there is no deviation for a closure to exonerate and, equally, the rider cannot convert its absence into a deviation the trace does not show. It is named here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. No other artifact falls below weight 1.0.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. The deciding fact — that the excess does not meet the POL-RD-01 threshold — is carried by the GPS trace (60.91 km) and the trip record (58.4 km optimal), both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. Confidence is set at 0.90, comfortably above the 0.70 escalation floor, and none of the POL-RD-10(1)-(8) triggers fires: identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, timestamps agree, every charge line has a trace counterpart, and no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact. This is a ruling, not an escalation, and no clause on this record mandates a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
